title: Juste Jocyte drama: Why Valkyries must resolve situation with prized rookie - CBS Sports
description: Jocytė, the No. 5 pick in the 2025 draft, didn't see much time this season, but could be an important part of the
body:
Jocytė, the No. 5 pick in the 2025 draft, didn't see much time this season, but could be an important part of the Valkyries' future
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:44 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Golden State Valkyries won their first championship less than two weeks ago, but what should have been a celebratory and drama-free offseason has already been turned on its head by an explosive interview from Juste Jocyte, the No. 5 overall pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft, in her native Lithuania. Speaking to BasketNews, Jocytė expressed some doubt about her future in the Bay Area after a frustrating campaign on a personal level. Jocytė, the first draft pick in Valkyries history, barely played during her rookie season. She averaged 3.1 points and 1.1 assists in 8.1 minutes over 16 appearances, and played five total minutes in the playoffs. As the offseason unfolds, let's take a closer look at what we know about the situation. What did Jocytė say?Jocytė spoke in Lithuanian, so we only have the English translation of her quotes. It's therefore unfair to quote those translations directly, but here is a summary of her key points:
Jocytė had mixed feelings about the season because she didn't get to play much en route to the title.Jocytė is unsure about returning to the Valkyries due to limited playing time and a fraught relationship with coach Natalie Nakase.Jocytė never fully understood why she was out of the rotation and received different explanations throughout the season.Jocytė lamented a lack of communication from Nakase and general manager Ohemaa Nyanin.Valkyries beat writer Kenzo Fukada subsequently reported that Jocytė and her camp were frustrated that Nakase "wasn't consistent with her reasoning to the media regarding why she didn't play, and that Nakase cycling through different reasons for not giving Jocytė playing time made it difficult for her to decipher what she needed to do to climb the rotation."How have the Valkyries addressed the situation?Neither Nakase nor Nyanin has done any media since Jocytė's interview, but Valkyries owner Joe Lacob did speak about the situation with Tim Kawakami on his podcast.  "I kind of understand. She's competitive and would like to win and didn't play," Lacob said. "But you know, she's also only 20. We had a pretty great roster, very deep. I think she can be a very good player, and we'd really love to have her back. 
"I think she will certainly earn a lot more playing time in the future. I can understand there are emotional moments in the moment. She didn't get to play as much as she wanted to, and that's understandable." 
        
            
                What's next for the Valkyries? Why Golden State could add star free agent to championship core
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Why does all of this matter?Why all the hullabaloo about someone who didn't play on a championship team? Well, Jocytė is not your usual end-of-the-bench player who's just filling out the roster. Jocytė was a phenom growing up in Europe. She led Lithuania to a silver medal at the U16 European championships as a 13-year-old and turned pro at 14 with ASVEL Lyon. She became the youngest player to appear in France's Ligue Féminine de Basketball and EuroBasket Women. 
Before coming over to the WNBA, she led Lyon to the semifinals in EuroCup Women 2025 (along with Dominique Malonga) and helped Spar Girona to a fourth-place finish in EuroLeague Women 2026. Standing 6 feet, she's a big, left-handed guard who can play with or without the ball, and has already proven herself on the biggest stages as a teenager. Jocytė is still only 20, and would be starting her junior year if she went the collegiate route. She still has a lot of potential, and the Valkyries made a big investment in her when they selected her No. 5 overall in 2025. Jocytė is under contract through 2028, with a team option for 2029, and will make less than $400K next season. While the Valkyries have plenty of cap space right now, that may not be the case moving forward if they end up signing another max player in free agency this winter. Regardless, having cheap, young talent will be crucial as they try to extend their title window. And even the Valkyries, a team that traded the No. 8 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft for two second-rounders, will not want to punt on a former No. 5 pick. 
What options do Jocytė and the Valkyries have?Valkyries waive JocytėJocytė's contract is unprotected, so the Valkyries could waive her ahead of next season for no cost to open up a roster spot and some additional cap space. That seems highly unlikely. Valkyries trade JocytėIf Jocytė makes it clear that she doesn't want to play for the Valkyries again, they could look to trade her this offseason. Given her age, potential and cheap salary, you have to imagine that a number of teams would be interested, but what would they be willing to give up? Determining Jocytė's trade value is tricky, especially after her comments, which removed much of the Valkyries' leverage. Jocytė sits out the 2027 seasonLithuania has been selected as one of the hosts for EuroBasket Women 2027, meaning the country has automatically qualified for the tournament, set for June 16-27. Jocytė was already going to miss a chunk of the 2027 WNBA season to participate in EuroBasket. 
What if she skips out on the WNBA entirely in order to prepare for one of the biggest competitions in her career and her country's history? That is not inconceivable, especially if she remains on the Valkyries' roster heading into the spring. The Valkyries would retain her rights in that scenario, though that wouldn't mean much with expansion looming. Jocytė returns to the ValkyriesOf course, it's always possible that Jocytė and the Valkyries smooth things over and she returns to the team next season. Again, she's still only 20, has so much room to grow and is on a rookie contract. There's a world where she becomes part of the Valkyries' rotation next season and an important piece of their future. More expansion drafts loomingIt's worth noting that this is the last offseason without an expansion draft until 2030. The Cleveland Sirens will join the league in 2028, followed by the Detroit franchise in 2029 and the Philadelphia franchise in 2030. Therefore, the Valkyries have extra pressure to sort out the Jocytė saga this offseason. 
Otherwise, they'd either have to protect her in the coming expansion drafts -- potentially ahead of more important players -- or risk leaving her unprotected and losing her for nothing.

title: Blue Jays executive responds to Anthony Santander's 'extremely disappointing' anti-Muslim social media posts - CBS Sports
description: Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins said he told Santander that he needed to address his comments publicly
body:
Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins said he told Santander that he needed to address his comments publicly
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:14 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins had strong words Tuesday in reaction to Anthony Santander's anti-Muslim social media posts that he has since deleted."There really aren't words to express my level of disappointment," Atkins said from the GM meetings on Tuesday, via Sportsnet. "Anything exacerbating some level of hate, anti-Islamic, is just extremely concerning and extremely disappointing."I also talked to Anthony about his lack of awareness, realizing that he has a very large microphone, what that meant. We're working exceptionally hard internally to ensure, and we have been, that it's a safe environment, that baseball is for everyone. It's very important to us. It's a part of our organizational values and his behavior did not align with that."  Santander, a native Venezuelan, shared social media videos in the wake of the U.S. midterm elections last week, including one where a Christian pastor said, "there is no such thing as kind Muslims." Another implied that Sharia law would be imposed in the U.S. following the election of Abdul El-Sayed to the Senate. Santander has since taken down the videos from his social media pages. In the aftermath, the team released the following statement: 
"Baseball is for everyone, and the Blue Jays have created an inclusive experience where all fans feel welcome at our ballpark. Individual comments do not represent our organization's values and beliefs."It's unclear whether Santander plans to address the matter publicly, but Atkins said he "told him that I thought he needed to and that he should." As far as personal conversations with Santander, Atkins said, "I expressed my level of concern. I believe he felt it. I know he feels badly. But I don't want to speak for him."  
Santander was signed as an amateur free agent out of Venezuela in 2011 when he was 16. He signed a free agent deal with the Blue Jays prior to the 2025 season; injuries have held him to just 54 games in the past two seasons.

title: College Football Playoff Rankings: Georgia moves to No. 1 as Alabama, UCLA join top four in second release - CBS Sports
description: The second College Football Playoff rankings are out, setting the stage for the final three weeks of the regular
body:
The second College Football Playoff rankings are out, setting the stage for the final three weeks of the regular season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:38 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The second edition of the College Football Playoff Rankings was released Tuesday night with Georgia taking over the No. 1 spot. Last week's No. 1 team, Miami (FL), fell to Notre Dame in one of the most-anticipated games of the 2026 season on Saturday night in Week 10. Simultaneously, the Bulldogs made an emphatic statement by demolishing Ole Miss on the road in Oxford, clearing the path for Kirby Smart and the Dawgs to sit atop the CFP Rankings heading into Week 11. Sitting at 8-1 (6-1 SEC) with three weeks left in the regular season, Georgia seems like a lock to make the 12-team bracket unless it stumbles mightily down this final stretch. Missouri, South Carolina and Georgia Tech -- one of the more notable disappointments of this season -- remain, plus a potential SEC Championship Game appearance. Should the Dawgs continue to play to the standard they've set for themselves in 2026, another appearance in the CFP lies ahead. Filling the void left by Georgia at the No. 2 spot is Utah (9-0, 6-0 Big 12) as Morgan Scalley continues to impress in his first season leading the Utes following Kyle Whittingham's departure. One of two unbeaten teams remaining at the FBS level, Utah is coming off its biggest win of the season, outlasting archrival BYU in the Holy War in Week 10. A tough test awaits Scalley and the Utes this week with a road trip to Arizona on tap. Rounding out the top five, Alabama moved to No. 3 on the heels of its win over LSU. Meanwhile, UCLA, one of two remaining unbeatens in the FBS, joined the top four and Notre Dame rose to No. 5 after its marquee win over Miami. 
With the 12-team playoff model granting automatic bids to the five highest-ranked conference champions, Boise State would take the last spot if the field were chosen today from the Group of Six level, as the Broncos come in at No. 24.College Football Playoff Rankings, Nov. 10~ First-round byeGeorgia (8-1) ~Utah (9-0) ~Alabama (7-2) ~UCLA (9-0) ~Notre Dame (8-1)Texas (7-2)Miami (8-1)Tennessee (7-2)Indiana (8-1)BYU (7-2)Kentucky (7-2)Texas Tech (8-1)Wake Forest (8-1)Houston (7-2)Iowa (7-2)Oregon (6-3)South Carolina (6-3)USC (7-2)Ole Miss (6-3)Ohio State (6-3)LSU (6-3)Missouri (6-3)Arizona (7-2)Boise State (8-1)Oklahoma State (6-3)Takeaways from second CFP RankingsThere's not near as much griping this week compared to last, now that we've received an overview of the selection committee's process this season and where teams initially fell with respect to "pods" and various clusters. Those 13 members wanted to see a signature win — or else — from Notre Dame against Miami, and the Fighting Irish delivered. Rising from No. 11 to No. 5 on Tuesday night is substantial and puts Marcus Freeman's team on the threshold of a first-round home game."We talked last week that Notre Dame had a lot of respect from the committee, a dominant team, but had yet to have the signature win, and they looked like the Notre Dame team that should be ranked No. 5. They were up 24-3 (on Miami)," CFP chair Hunter Yurachek said.
The biggest surprise was Indiana's five-spot drop to No. 9, despite not playing over the weekend. The selection committee starts from scratch every week, and their re-ranking of sorts did no favors to the Hoosiers, who host USC this weekend.Three SEC locksGeorgia's move to No. 1 was justified after the Bulldogs' 35-point rampage at Ole Miss. The Bulldogs are now No. 1 in game control and No. 2 in strength of record after that victory and have looked incredibly impressive since their upset loss to Auburn on Oct. 17.Widely considered the most overrated team in last week's initial reveal at No. 5, Alabama strengthened the selection committee's gut after the Crimson Tide's 31-13 win at LSU. Rated near the FBS leaders in strength of record, SOS and game control, grab the Sharpie for third-ranked Alabama, with Vanderbilt, Chattanooga and Auburn left to play.
Texas, now ranked sixth, is top-15 in every measurable metric this season after beating Missouri on the road, a distinction no other SEC team has at this point. The Longhorns also hold the key data point associated with a nation-leading four ranked wins. Steve Sarkisian has a chance at another Saturday at LSU. After taking out Ohio State in the non-conference and the victory at Tennessee, coupled with three straight wins since dropping two consecutive in October, Texas has margin for error to be an at-large pick even if it loses another.UCLA overlooked no moreAfter debuting at No. 8, UCLA moved to No. 4 in the second rankings. The metrics suggest the Bruins deserved to be this high considering their SOR (1st) and GC (9th), but a SOS slotted at No. 67 is not strong. Winning out assures UCLA of a spot in the Big Ten Championship, but not necessarily a top-4 seed. The Bruins on Friday night host Illinois, who's won four straight, before ending the campaign with Michigan and USC.Oregon leads three-loss teamsThe Ducks' win at Ohio State pushed them ahead of the Buckeyes, who suffered an eight-spot drop from No. 12. Oregon now holds three ranked wins this season, which is tied for second-most in the country behind Texas (4). South Carolina held off Texas A&M to win its fourth straight over the weekend and improved its CFP ranking to No. 17, up four spots from last week.
No. 16 Oregon (6-3)No. 17 South Carolina (6-3)No. 19 Ole Miss (6-3)No. 20 Ohio State (6-3)No. 21 LSU (6-3)ACC dramaMy biggest question entering this second reveal was where the selection committee would put previously top-ranked Miami. We saw them downgrade Ohio State after losing quarterback Julian Sayin to injury, so what would they do with Miami after Malachi Toney's unfortunate practice mishap leading to a loss in South Bend? A six-spot tumble is not justifiable when you consider the Hurricanes were the equivalent of a near-unanimous No. 1 a week. As for the ACC's shot at being a two-bid league, Wake Forest is bringing up the rear at No. 13. The Demon Deacons, who play at SMU on Saturday, are the only team ranked by the selection committee this week with just one victory this season over an opponent with a record above .500. By comparison, Texas has a nation-leading six such wins, while Miami has four (tops in the ACC) and more than Wake Forest, SMU and Duke combined.

title: College basketball winners, losers: Big early deficits doom No. 3 Illinois in loss at Texas Tech, No. 2 Duke - CBS Sports
description: The drama in Tuesday's loaded slate made it feel more like March than November
body:
The drama in Tuesday's loaded slate made it feel more like March than November
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:54 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Tuesday's college basketball schedule was heralded as one of the best nonconference days of the season. With close games, upsets and drama in marquee matchups, it's safe to say it lived up to the hype. No. 1 Florida, No. 2 Duke and No. 3 Illinois were all in action against quality opponents away from home. And two of the three went down in defeat.Florida came away with an 81-72 road win over in-state foe Florida State to move to 2-0, while Duke received a wake-up call with a 79-73 upset loss to No. 5 Michigan State in the Champions Classic. The Fighting Illini weren't so lucky in their road game at No. 16 Texas Tech. The Red Raiders jumped out to a 20-point lead in the first half and held off a rally from Illinois behind 20 points from Cruz Davis in Texas Tech's 74-68 victory. 
        
            
                Champions Classic NBA Draft guide: Who scouts will be watching in college basketball's high-profile showcase
                
                    Adam Finkelstein                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Not every team playing on Tuesday walked away feeling good after a win. Michael Malone's North Carolina squad only led by two points at halftime against Wyoming before pulling away in the second half for a 76-63 win. The Tar Heels also received an upset scare in their season-opener against Western Carolina last week before pulling away in the final minutesAfter an intense day of hoops, here are the biggest winners and losers from the slate.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Jeremy Fears Jr. shines vs. DukeFears was simply brilliant against Duke. He finished with a double-double (18 points and 11 assists). The way he controls the pace of the game and runs the offense, there are not many players in the sport who do it as well as he does. Fears is the best point guard in America. The way he sets up his teammates for good looks in transition and in half-court sets is unmatched. Fears showed why he was the CBS Sports Preseason POTY. -- Cameron Salerno

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Duke receives a wake-up callTuesday should serve as a wake-up call for Duke. Not only did Michigan State beat Duke, but it also dominated from start to finish in the most impressive win by any team in college basketball this season. The Blue Devils couldn't buy a bucket in this game. Part of it was shot selection and the other part was Michigan State's defense, which was so good and physical that Duke couldn't get clean looks.The bad (maybe, good) news? Duke's schedule gets significantly harder during the next month. Duke faces UConn and Illinois this month. Duke will certainly be tested this season. This game should serve as an early measuring stick for Scheyer's team. -- CS

        
            
                Dismantling of Duke by Michigan State shows it might be time to recalibrate expectations for Blue Devils
                
                    Isaac Trotter                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Bad vibes for Kentucky already?Not only did Kentucky look disjointed and overmatched, it also looked timid and disinterested relative to the free-flowing and well-connected Jayhawks. The bench lacked energy, and it was hard not to consider the "what if" factor of Tyran Stokes. Kentucky heavily pursued Kansas' freshman phenom, who is a Louisville native. They lost that recruiting battle and lost out on a great player who brought strong vibes to the matchup. Stokes played with an obvious intensity and joy that was clearly missing from the Kentucky side. This wasn't as bad as bad as Kentucky's 94-59 neutral-site loss to Gonzaga last season. But it should be a wakeup call. Early in a critical third season for coach Mark Pope, UK has a lot to figure out. -- David Cobb
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Texas Tech records huge win over IllinoisYou could hear how loud the environment at Texas Tech was by sitting at home with your TV volume on. The atmosphere inside the arena sounded electric. Texas Tech recorded one of the most impressive wins of the season by taking down No. 3 Illinois. A rematch of this game sometime in March would be great when All-Americans on both sides (Illinois' David Mirkovic and Texas Tech's JT Toppin) are cleared to play. Nonetheless, Texas Tech should receive a sizeable boost in next week's AP poll after taking down the No. 3 team in the country. -- CS
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Tyran Stokes has elevatedWhen the top-rated freshman makes jumpers, Stokes is almost unstoppable. It's early in the cycle, but Stokes looks like a tier above the rest in the early 2027 NBA Draft discourse. The 6-foot-8 bullyball wing was phenomenal, totaling 23 points, 10 rebounds and four assists. Kentucky had absolutely no answer for the big dawg. -- Isaac Trotter

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: North Carolina receives a scare from WyomingFor the second time in three games, it got scary for North Carolina. In Malone's debut at UNC, the Tar Heels were in a close game with Western Carolina before pulling away down the stretch. Against Wyoming, UNC led by only two points at halftime before outscoring the Cowboys by double digits in the second half. With a game against Georgia looming at home later this week, the Tar Heels will have to play better or risk not escaping with a win. -- CS
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Florida picks up win over another in-state rivalFlorida played a C+ game against Miami last week and came away with a double-digit win. Tuesday's showdown against in-state foe Florida State was a lot more of a hostile environment than the very pro-Gators crowd Todd Golden's team played in front of during a season opener against Miami in Tampa. FSU made things very interesting in the second half, cutting the deficit to four with less than seven minutes remaining. However, Florida was able to close things out behind another double-double (21 points and 10 rebounds) from star forward Thomas Haugh.Florida State played teams extremely tough during Year 1 of Luke Loucks' tenure at his alma mater. This game showed the Seminoles will make some real noise in the ACC this season. -- CS

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Vanderbilt makes a statement vs. MemphisVanderbilt made a statement with a 105-81 win vs. Memphis, which was off to a surprising 2-0 start under coach Penny Hardaway. Washington State transfer Ace Glass III knocked down five 3-pointers and finished with 23 points. Meanwhile, preseason All-American Tyler Tanner scored 17 points on 8-for-14 shooting. Vanderbilt is now 3-0, with double-digit wins over Wake Forest and Memphis on the resume. Memphis began the season with an upset win over Iowa State, but couldn't take down Vanderbilt on the road. -- CS

title: CFP Rankings reaction: Alabama overrated, how did Indiana lose during a bye? - CBS Sports
description: The College Football Playoff committee is swinging big in 2026 with at least three moves they've never made befor
body:
The College Football Playoff committee is swinging big in 2026 with at least three moves they've never made before, including a stunning drop for idle Indiana
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:14 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Tennessee dominated Alabama head-to-head, and on Saturday the Volunteers beat top-10 Kentucky by four touchdowns.The College Football Playoff's selection committee was still not moved.Alabama climbed two spots to No. 3 in the second CFP Rankings on Tuesday night, making the Tide the highest-ranked, two-loss team in the country. It's the earliest a two-loss team has ever appeared in the committee's top four. Tennessee, which owns the same 7-2 record and the 26-10 victory against the Tide in Neyland Stadium, is No. 8.The gap is five spots after standing at eight slots a week ago. Alabama has been helped by the metrics the CFP utilizes in its selection process, selection committee chairman Hunter Yurachek said Tuesday. The Tide own the nation's No. 1 record strength and No. 1 schedule strength. "They have four what we call quality wins because we continue to call that win against Mississippi State earlier in the year when they had Kamario Taylor on their team; they were 4-0," he said on ESPN. "Alabama went there and won that game. Alabama, we believe, deserves to be the No. 3 team in the country."
Yup, Mississippi State is likely the motivating factor for ranking Alabama that high.Notre Dame won the biggest game of Week 10 and made the largest jump among the top 10, moving from No. 11 to No. 5 after beating previous No. 1 Miami. No team in the history of the CFP Rankings had gone from outside the top 10 into the top five in one week.But did Notre Dame deserve to be outside the top 10 in the first place?The committee continues to cling to the new strength-of-conference data that was introduced this season. Nine SEC teams are in the top 25, with seven ranked higher than in this week's AP poll. None were ranked lower than their spots in the AP poll.  
Four SEC teams were ranked at least three spots higher than in the AP. And for those who are looking ahead to the 24-team CFP next season: nine SEC teams would be in the field and the conference would own four of the eight first-round byes. In another interesting twist, Texas Tech would go from the first team out of the 12-team playoff to hosting a playoff game.The 10 teams the committee has ranked lower than the AP all come from outside the SEC: Boise State, Indiana, USC, Notre Dame, Miami, Texas Tech, Wake Forest and Arizona, plus New Mexico and SMU, which the AP ranks and the committee does not.Once again, the SEC is the rankings king.Let's take a look at who is overrated, frustrated and underrated heading into Week 11:

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Overrated: AlabamaWe get it, the SEC is the deepest conference in the country, but why is Alabama ranked so differently than its other counterparts in the league? The committee has Alabama four spots higher than the AP does. That is the same gap as a week ago, and it is the widest for any team in the top 15.Alabama is 3-2 against the committee's current top 25 with wins at Kentucky (45-17), against South Carolina (49-18) and at LSU (31-13). Only Texas, at 4-0, has more top-25 wins among the top 13. Both of Alabama's losses came against top-eight teams, including a 20-17 home defeat to No. 1 Georgia.The case for No. 3 is just not a strong argument. Those three wins have lost their shine. Kentucky has now been beaten by 28 points twice. South Carolina still has three losses. The worst team helping their ranking is LSU, the team they just got beat 31-13 on the road last week. LSU is 0-3 against the top 25, and it's easy to argue the Tigers do not belong in the top 25. 
Alabama also sits ahead of unbeaten UCLA and a one-loss Notre Dame team that just beat No. 1.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Frustrated: IndianaIndiana sat at home and rested this week, and their reward for the much-needed breather was a five-spot fall to No. 9.That's the biggest drop for an idle team in the CFP's 13 seasons. The largest drop for an idle team previously was three spots: Nebraska (2014) and Penn State (2022).
It's understandable that the Hoosiers would fall in the rankings after Notre Dame and Utah's wins, but five spots? Come on. That's just punishment. It didn't help that the Big Ten teams on Indiana's schedule this season were a combined 0-8 last week. The Hoosiers were "probably a victim of having a bye week at the wrong time," Yurachek said Tuesday.You can bet Curt Cignetti will have his Indiana squad fired up when No. 18 USC comes to Bloomington on Saturday.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Overrated: MissouriSeven teams with three losses are ranked, with four from the SEC: South Carolina (No. 17), Ole Miss (No. 19), LSU (No. 21) and Missouri (No. 22). They are a combined 3-9 against the current top 25, and two of the three wins belong to Ole Miss -- against LSU and Missouri.LSU and Missouri are a combined 0-5 against the CFP's top 25. Missouri lost to unranked Mississippi State (though the Bulldogs were ranked at the time with a healthy Kamario Taylor), lost 31-3 at Ole Miss and lost by 14 at home to Texas on Saturday. The AP voters did not rank the Tigers.It's difficult to say Ole Miss is overrated, but two of its three losses were blowouts. Ole Miss lost 42-7 at home to Georgia on Saturday and is still in the top 20. The Rebels also have a 52-28 loss at unranked Florida, which fell out of the rankings this week.
South Carolina has caught fire with a four-game winning streak -- and they were jumped by three-loss Oregon this week after the Ducks beat Ohio State on the road. The Gamecocks' placement is understandable.Still, all of them are ranked ahead of an 8-1 team the committee has yet to rank -- New Mexico.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Underrated: TennesseeThe Vols are 2-2 against the top 25 with wins against No. 3 Alabama and No. 11 Kentucky by a combined 44 points. Their two losses came by a combined six points: 20-17 vs. No. 6 Texas and 27-24 at No. 17 South Carolina.
Alabama's argument rests on one more top-25 win and one common opponent. The Tide beat South Carolina by 31. Tennessee lost in Columbia by three. So, that could be an argument, but the committee's own protocol lists head-to-head results second among the four principles it applies when teams look comparable. Results against common opponents are third.Tennessee is still in great position to reach the CFP, but a first-round bye appears off the table. The Vols play at Texas A&M on Saturday and host LSU on Nov. 21. Alabama has already beaten both.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Underrated: Texas TechThe Red Raiders are the first team out at No. 12, two spots lower than voters had them in the AP poll. They are 8-1 overall and 2-0 against the top 25, with wins over No. 14 Houston and No. 23 Arizona. That is as many top-25 wins as Kentucky with one fewer loss and nothing resembling a 28-point defeat.
The blemish is a 37-24 loss at unranked Cincinnati, and a 53-48 escape against West Virginia last week did not help. The Red Raiders can add a third ranked win Saturday at No. 25 Oklahoma State, which entered the rankings this week.Wake Forest at No. 13 makes sense, even at 8-1. Its only game against a ranked opponent was a 13-point loss to Miami, which tumbled six spots to No. 7 this week. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Underrated: New Mexico and Boise StateNew Mexico is 8-1, ranked No. 23 by the AP and unranked by the committee for the second straight week. The Lobos' only loss was 14-6 at Oklahoma on Sept. 19, and the Sooners have since beaten Texas and won at Florida. New Mexico has not played a team in the top 25, but the Lobos are behind Missouri, which is 0-2 against the top 25 with an additional loss to an unranked opponent (Mississippi State).         Chicago White Sox manager Will Venable and Brewers manager Pat Murphy were named the Managers of the Year in their respective leagues on Tuesday night as part of the BBWAA's awards week. Murphy is the first manager to ever win the award in three consecutive seasons.The annual awards, which also include Manager of the Year, Reliever of the Year, Cy Young and MVP, are voted on by 30 members of the Baseball Writers Association of America (that's two per MLB city in each league). Votes were submitted before the beginning of the playoffs, meaning that only regular-season contributions are taken into account.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    National League: Pat Murphy, BrewersMurphy, manager of the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers, has been voted the National League Manager of the Year, the Baseball Writers Association of America announced on Tuesday. He is the first person to win three consecutive Manager of the Year awards and the tenth person with three Manager of the Year wins in total.Ballots for the BBWAA's awards are submitted between the end of the regular season and the beginning of the postseason. They are regular-season awards and Milwaukee's World Series win did not factor into the voting.
Of course, Murphy did not need the World Series win to boost his Manager of the Year case. He guided the small-market Brewers to baseball's best record (103-59) and run differential (+214) during the regular season, and their fourth consecutive NL Central title. Their 103 wins are a franchise record and baseball's most since 2023.Manager1st2nd3rdPointsPat Murphy, Brewers2073124Walt Weiss, Braves716386Don Mattingly, Phillies131125Craig Stammen, Padres211124Dave Roberts, Dodgers217Craig Counsell, Cubs13Don Kelly, Pirates11Murphy just completed his third season as Brewers manager and has three Manager of the Year wins to show for it. Bobby Cox (2004-05), Kevin Cash (2020-21), and Stephen Vogt (2024-25) are the only others with two consecutive Manager of the Year awards. Vogt was not an American League Manager of the Year finalist this season.Prior to Murphy's threepeat here, the Brewers had never had a Manager of the Year winner. He's won the award now three times in three years at the helm.
Atlanta Braves manager Walt Weiss and Philadelphia Phillies manager Don Mattingly finished behind Murphy in the voting. Mattingly took over as an interim after the Phillies fired Rob Thomson on April 28. Philadelphia had baseball's fourth-best record after the managerial change. Weiss guided the Braves to the NL East title.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    American League: Will Venable, White SoxVenable, who helped orchestrate a 24-win year-to-year improvement and guided the team to its first postseason berth since 2021, has been named the American League Manager of the Year, the Baseball Writers Association of America announced on Tuesday. He beat out Tampa Bay Rays manager Kevin Cash and Boston Red Sox manager Chad Tracy.The White Sox went 84-78 in 2026 after going 60-102 in 2025 and a hideous 41-121 in 2024. Those 121 losses are the record in baseball's Modern Era (since 1900). Venable's White Sox are the first team in history to reach the postseason after losing at least 100 games in the previous two seasons (they also lost 101 games in 2023).
The huge steps forward seem to be what secured the award for Venable. He took over in 2025 and the White Sox improved by 19 wins that season, only to turn around and improve by 24 more wins this past season. They were arguably the most surprising playoff team in 2026 and Venable gets his due here. Manager1st2nd3rdPointsWill Venable, White Sox15113111Kevin Cash, Rays1212298Chad Tracy, Red Sox351747Stephen Vogt, Guardians169Aaron Boone, Yankees114Joe Espada, Astros11Venable joins the following White Sox manager of the year winners: Ozzie Guillen, 2005Jerry Manuel, 2000Gene Lamont, 1993Jeff Torborg, 1990Tony La Russa, 1983Cash finishes as the runner-up in a very close vote. body:
New York reportedly pulled an offer of two draft picks for the Colts star, leaving the division-leading offense in the hands of a confident Skattebo

        The New York Giants decided to stand pat at the NFL trade deadline. While they showed interest in adding a defensive tackle like Jeffery Simmons and a running back such as Jonathan Taylor, John Harbaugh and Joe Schoen elected not to ship off valuable draft capital as the Giants prepare for the second half of the season.New York was one of several teams that could have benefitted from a new running back like Taylor. Fox Sports reported that the Giants offered the Indianapolis Colts second- and fifth-round picks for their star back, but eventually took that offer off the table.No one may be happier about that than running back Cam Skattebo, who will now still be responsible for the bulk of the carries for the Giants. In the locker room after the trade deadline passed, Skattebo was asked about holding onto his starting spot after the Giants' pursuit of Taylor ended. "I've been that guy," Skattebo said. "Obviously, we had that one-week hiccup where I got in trouble. That was it. I came back that next week and handled business. They know what I'm capable of. They know what I can do."
The Giants couldn't reach a deal with the Colts, who were likely asking too high a price for Taylor. Now, New York will stick with what it has. "You don't want to make a bad deal," Harbaugh said on Tuesday, per NJ.com. "You make a bad deal, that doesn't make you better. That makes you worse. Sometimes, the best deal is the deal that you don't make."We're willing to pay a price to make our team better. But it's got to be something that really makes our team better. It's got to be worth it. I would want a player that we love."
Skattebo has rushed for 418 yards and two touchdowns in seven games played this season. It's already been a dramatic year that has included a benching, followed by a career performance. Skattebo was given zero touches in Week 6 following his costly overtime fumble in the eventual tie against the Washington Commanders the week prior. However, he bounced back to rush for a career-high 124 yards and a touchdown against the Houston Texans in Week 7. It was an epic redemption game, which included a play where Skattebo broke loose for 42 yards in overtime to set up New York's fourth win of the season. 
Skattebo suffered a hamstring injury on this play, which forced him to miss the Week 9 win over the Philadelphia Eagles, but he's expected to return this Thursday against the Commanders.
"You've seen what I can do," Skattebo said. "When I come out, and I'm ready to play football, I can be one of the most dangerous backs in the league. Simple as that."The 5-2-1 Giants are currently two games ahead of the Dallas Cowboys in the NFC East. Maybe adding the player who has recorded the fifth-most rushing yards per game (88.8) in NFL history could have taken the Giants' offense to another level, but Skattebo clearly believes he's capable of being an effective bell cow.

From Italy's biggest teams to America's biggest stars, Serie A has it all, and Paramount+ is the home for every minute of the action until a Scudetto winner is crowned.   AC Milan's star is no longer Christian Pulisic Ruben Amorim's AC Milan come from two positive league wins against Inter and Genoa. The Rossoneri are back on track right now fighting for one of the top spots in the Serie A standings and their new star is Italian striker Alphadjo Cisse, who has already scored eight goals in 13 games played between the league and the UEFA Europa League matches. Downs now goes from catching passes from Daniel Jones, whose 82.3 passer rating ranks 34th out of 35 qualified quarterbacks this season, to catching passes from Patrick Mahomes, a three-time Super Bowl MVP. That's why he tweeted the gif of Vince Carter expressing gratitude in reaction to the news that he is now a Chief.He quickly followed up that post by tweeting, "I am beyond grateful and blessed for my time in Indy. Nothing but love for the [horse] Shoe."
So how did the Colts and Chiefs make out in this trade deadline deal? Here is a look at the grade for each squad.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kansas City Chiefs: B+The Chiefs (6-2) are always in win-now mode, with Mahomes (31 years old), tight end Travis Kelce (37), defensive tackle Chris Jones (32), defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo (66) and head coach Andy Reid (68) getting up there in age. Kelce, Rashee Rice, who is coming back from an offseason knee surgery, and former first-round pick Xavier Worthy haven't been getting the job done.
Kansas City is averaging 117.5 receiving yards per game by wide receivers this season, which is the fewest of the Mahomes era (since 2018) and ranks 28th in the NFL this season. That's why the Chiefs went out and traded for Downs. The 25-year-old Downs has been a weapon out of the slot since entering the league as a third-round pick in 2023: His 1,995 yards receiving out of the slot are the second most in the entire NFL in the span of his career, trailing only Detroit Lions All-Pro wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (2,160). Most receiving yards from the slot, since 2023Receiving yards from the slotAmon-Ra St. Brown2,160Josh Downs*1,995CeeDee Lamb1,970Trey McBride1,966Jaxon Smith-Njigba1,766* Downs was drafted in the third round of the 2023 NFL DraftSure, Downs is a rental playing out the final year of his rookie contract in 2026, but Kansas City was desperate. Plus, if Downs builds a nice rapport with Mahomes, this deal could lead to a second contract come the 2027 offseason. It's also a huge win that the Chiefs didn't have to part with any Day 2 draft capital. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Indianapolis Colts: ADowns requested a trade, and he is playing out the final year of his rookie contract. There was no chance he would be open to re-signing with Indianapolis in the 2027 offseason, especially with the Colts set to dive headfirst into a rebuild with a new general manager. The Colts did well to get multiple early Day 3 draft picks for a disgruntled player who already had one foot out the door.

Jared Goff lost all seven rookie starts, Lamar Jackson went 6-1 and made the playoffs. Now Mendoza faces the same challenge.

        In 2016, the Rams were 4-5 when they benched Case Keenum and handed the offense to No. 1 overall pick Jared Goff. He lost all seven of his starts, threw five touchdowns and seven interceptions, and LA finished 4-12. Jeff Fisher was fired with three games remaining, the Rams hired Sean McVay that offseason, and the rest is history.Two years later, the Ravens were also 4-5 when Lamar Jackson, the final pick of the first round in 2018, replaced an injured Joe Flacco. He won six of his first seven starts, and Baltimore won the AFC North before losing to the Chargers in the wild-card round. Jackson threw just five touchdowns, but his ability to run transformed everything about the offense.Same record. Same point in the season. Two completely different outcomes.And now comes Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 pick in April's draft, who inherits a 4-5 Raiders team after Las Vegas traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota on Tuesday for a third-round pick. Mendoza will make his first start Sunday against the Seahawks, and while it's tempting to think nine weeks on the bench may have helped prepare him for what's next, history suggests it could be a little more complicated than that.What happens when rookie QBs don't start until midseason?Since 2000, 148 quarterbacks have started at least one game as NFL rookies. Just 22 made their first start between Weeks 10 and 13, and their collective debuts were not pretty. 
They completed just 53.8% of their passes, averaged 5.8 yards per attempt and threw interceptions on 5.3% of their dropbacks – the worst marks of any group. Only five of those 22 won their debuts, and their interception rate was more than 1.6 times that of rookies who started in Week 1.How rookie QBs performed in their first career start, 2000-2025First start came in:Comp. %YPAINT rateWin %Week 157.6%6.13.3%29.7%Weeks 2-558.4%6.43.6%25.7%Weeks 6-956.3%6.43.8%27.3%Weeks 10-1353.8%5.85.3%22.7%Weeks 14-1856.4%6.13.5%37.5%Source: TruMediaOf course, circumstances matter. Some quarterbacks sat because they weren't ready. Others played because the starter got hurt or was ineffective. But the takeaway remains: Sitting for half a season doesn't guarantee a smoother transition to the top of the depth chart.What happened to the teams that turned to rookies?Five teams had winning records when they turned to a rookie in Weeks 10-13. They were a combined 30-19 before the change and went 10-20 afterward. The 17 teams with losing records fared slightly better when they installed a rookie under center, improving their winning percentage from 28.9% to 33.7% – though they still lost twice as often as they won.Team performance before and after a rookie's first start, Weeks 10-13Team entering debut had a:QBsBeforeAfterWin % afterWinning record530-1910-2033.3%Losing record1748-11834-6733.7%Total2278-13744-8733.6%Source: TruMediaOnly three of those 22 teams made the playoffs. The 2011 Texans turned to T.J. Yates after injuries to Matt Schaub and Matt Leinart. The 2017 Bills benched Tyrod Taylor for Nathan Peterman despite sitting at 5-4. Peterman threw five interceptions in the first half of his debut, Taylor reclaimed the job at halftime, and Buffalo eventually made the playoffs with Taylor back under center.Jackson was different. Baltimore initially needed him because Flacco was injured, but he played so well that they stuck with him even after Flacco was healthy. Obviously, that's a blueprint the Raiders would love to follow, but it's fair to say the organizational infrastructure isn't quite there yet.And then there are the more immediate concerns for the Raiders rookie…The schedule isn't doing Mendoza any favorsMendoza's first three starts come against Seattle, Denver and Cleveland, which also happen to be three of the league's best defenses. The schedule gets less daunting after a Week 13 bye, though matchups against the Broncos and Chiefs make up two of the Raiders; final four games. So yeah.There is a bigger issue: Mendoza could play well and still lose a bunch of games, and Vegas' first nine weeks help explain why.The Raiders' biggest problem isn't their rookie QBKirk Cousins wasn't the reason for all the losing when Vegas traded him. He had thrown 20 touchdowns and just eight interceptions, and the team was averaging 25.4 points per game. Their passing offense ranks fifth in yards per game and ninth in EPA per play, so Mendoza isn't walking into a no-win situation.The problems lie everywhere else. Las Vegas ranks dead last in yards per carry (2.9), 31st in rushing yards per game (71.3) and 30th in rushing success rate. The defense hasn't been much better, allowing 35.7 points per game over the last six weeks, five of them losses.That's a tough combination for any quarterback, future Hall of Famer or fresh face of the franchise. Kubiak's system can help, but even the best-designed offense needs a run game that provides some balance. Back in June, I wrote that Mendoza might be the most NFL-ready quarterback in the class but had landed in the least quarterback-friendly situation. My rookie QB model had him completing 61.4% of his passes, averaging 6.6 yards per attempt with an 82.1 passer rating.Which brings us back to Goff and Jackson.They started their careers headed in opposite directions, yet both eventually became two of the NFL's best quarterbacks. Goff didn't reach his current level until Detroit surrounded him with a strong offensive line, dependable running game and playmakers (and early on, Ben Johnson). Baltimore built its offense around Jackson's unique abilities rather than asking him to become something he wasn't.The Raiders already have their quarterback of the future. Mendoza has eight games to show what he can do, but whether he goes 0-8, 6-2 or somewhere in between won't tell us much about the quarterback he could become. His job is to prove he belongs. The organization's job is to make sure he has a chance to succeed.

How to bet on horse racing: Most popular types of wagers There are plenty of different wagering options available on each race. We will go through the three traditional bets – Win, Place and Show – as well as the combinations of each. Below are horse racing betting tips that identify bet types and the differences between the odds found at sportsbook and racing odds.  Each horse will have different odds for each bet type. These odds let you know the horse's expected return on each individual bet type. It's important to note that the odds on each horse fluctuate constantly and payouts are calculated based on the final odds, not the exact odds from the time you place your bet, a major difference from betting on other sports.               Differences in horse racing odds vs. sportsbook odds             Horse racing odds rely on pari-mutuel wagering, which is a system that pools together all of the money bet on each market up until the race begins. The track and the books take a certain percentage or rake for their operations (the Takeout), and the remainder of the pool is then divided among the winning ticket holders. The takeout is divided between the house (track) and horsemen, including race purses.               What is particularly unique about this system for those who are accustomed to betting on sports is that your odds can shift after you place the bet until they lock when the race begins. On sports betting apps, if you bet something at 10-1 and it later moves to 8-1, you still receive the 10-1 payout. In horse racing, your payout will change based on the way the market moves to create the final odds. The final odds you'll receive are determined by how much is bet on each horse and the Takeout.              The standard horse racing unit for win, place, or show bets is $2.                         Win             The win bet is simply betting on which horse will come in first place. Using the 2026 Herbie Dyke Stakes as an example, the winner was Legarto and finished with 12-5 odds. A $2 Win bet paid $6.80, a product of the standard $4.80 for a 12-5 payout on a $2 bet, plus your original $2 wager amount back.                          Place             The Place bet allows you to wager on whether a horse will finish first or second in a race, meaning two Place bets will pay out on each race. This gives you a greater chance of winning, but lowers your odds on the horse if they place.              Using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as the example again, a $2 Place bet on the No. 18 horse only returned $7.50 compared to the $17.96 for a Win bet. But also, a $2 Place bet on the No. 8 horse (Journalism), who was the favorite but came in second, paid $4.94 while the Win bet lost.                           Show             A Show bet is a highly conservative betting option. You are wagering on whether a horse will finish in the top three positions. That means three Show bets will pay out each race. For example, a $2 Show bet on a 10-1 winner returned $4. As one might expect, show bet odds are far less favorable than win bet odds, making them one of the more conservative wagers available in horse racing.                           Win/Place             Additionally, you can combine these bets on each horse when you're placing your wagers. That means if you want to bet on a horse to win and place, you can do that. A $2 Win/Place bet really means you're betting $4 – a $2 Win bet and a $2 Place bet. If the horse you bet on wins, you will win both bets. If the horse finishes second, you would only win the Place bet.                           Place/Show             The same is available for a Place/Show bet, where a $2 Place/Show bet would be $4 wagered on a $2 Place bet and a $2 Show bet. If your horse finishes first or second, you would win both, but if it finishes third, you would only win the Show bet.                           Win/Place/Show (Across The Board)              Lastly, you can bet on all three options in what is often referred to as an Across The Board bet. A $2 Across The Board bet would really be $6 wagered – $2 on Win, $2 on Place, and $2 on Show. If you make an Across The Board bet and your horse wins, you pay out on all three wagers.              It's important to note that betting on Win/Place/Show combinations may not result in a net return even if one of the bets pays. For example, at the 2024 Kentucky Derby, an Across The Board bet on the 11 horse would've returned just $5.58 on $6 wagered.                           The most popular horse racing bet types             Many horse racing bettors place exotic bets to try to predict where multiple horses will finish in a race. These combination wagers offer the chance for bigger payouts, but come with a lower probability of winning (just like same game parlays in sports betting).              It is important to note that, unlike sports betting, there is no standard odds calculation to use for determining exotic payouts. Because of parimutuel wagering, odds can fluctuate until the race begins based on which horses are taking the most action. Additionally, live horse racing betting is available, adding another layer of entertainment for those watching races as they take place.               Exactas             An exacta bet in horse racing functions the same as it does across other sports. The bettor must pick the exact finishing order. For example, if someone wants to place an exacta bet with two horses, they must select each horse and where it will finish exactly. Once again using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as an example, a $2 exacta on the No. 18 and No. 8 horses (who closed with final odds of 7-1 and almost 3-1) paid $48.32. This style of betting can be seen in plenty of other sports, especially in futures betting.  Exotics winnings will vary based on the number of horses in the race, the odds of the top-finishing horses, and the size of the pool. For example, the field for the 2024 Kentucky Derby saw a longer shot horse win, so the exacta pool paid $258.56 -- significantly more than the 2025 Derby.                           Trifectas             This horse racing wager is placing a bet on the exact order of the top-three finishers in a race. A straight trifecta will pay handsomely, but is extremely difficult to hit. Trifecta payouts are often shown for $0.50 bets, but some will show for $1 bets as well. The payout screen will tell you which, but that's important to note so you're aware of how much you are getting back.              The 2025 Kentucky Derby Trifecta paid $231.12 on a $1 Trifecta bet.                           Superfectas             Superfecta bets try to predict the exact order of the top-four finishers in a horse race. The superfecta payout is usually shown for a $1 bet. For the 2025 Kentucky Derby, a $1 superfecta that added the fourth-place No. 3 horse to the trifecta paid $1,682.27.                          Super High 5             Some books will allow you to bet on the top-five finishers in their exact order in what is called a Super High 5 bet. Those payouts will again be shown for a $1 wager. The odds of hitting a Super High 5, especially in a large field race, are exceptionally low. They are equivalent to multi-leg futures parlays in other forms of sports betting.  The 2025 Kentucky Derby's $1 Super High Five paid $38,405.96.                          Box             A box bet allows you to have every possible combination for exotics. If you think you know which two horses will hit the exacta but are not sure of their specific order, you can box it. The same goes for trifectas and superfectas. The more horses you box together, the lower your total profits on the payout will be.              For example, a three-horse exacta box bet costs $12 to bet, as you are betting $2 on all six potential combinations between those three horses:             $2 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 3 second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 1 in first and No. 3 in secondYou can do the same for Trifectas and Superfectas, but at exponentially escalating costs. A $1 Trifecta Box with three horses is six combinations, so $6 wagered:             $1 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 1 in first, No. 3 in second, No. 2 in first$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 2 in third$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 1 in firstFrom there, four horses in a $1 trifecta box is 24 combinations for $24 wagered. Five horses make 60 possible combinations for $60.              A $1 Superfecta box of four horses is $24 wagered, five horses is $120 wagered and six horses is $360 wagered.                           How to bet on horse racing: Multi-race wagers             While those exotics offer a variety of options for betting on individual races, you can also bet on multiple races at the same track in various ways. These combination wagers pay out based on the betting pool, allowing you to choose a handful of horses you're confident in throughout the day to increase your potential payout.                           Daily Double             The Daily Double is exactly what it sounds like: Betting on back-to-back race winners from that day. The odds for Daily Doubles vary based on the odds for the individual horses you bet and the overall Daily Double betting pool. As an example, the $2 Daily Double at Horseshoe Indianapolis on April 15, 2025 from the first two races with the 7 horse in the first race (went off at 1-1 odds) and the 4 horse in the second race (went off at 3-5 odds) paid $8.              Once the first race ends, the payouts for each potential Daily Double will be shown under a "Will Pays" tab on the next race's betting screen.                           Pick-3, Pick-4, Pick-5 and Pick-6             Along with the Daily Double, there are more options for betting the winner of multiple races in a row at the same track. The Pick-3 is picking the winner in three consecutive races, the Pick-4 in four consecutive races, and so on for the Pick-5 and Pick-6.             Like exotics, the pool amount and the odds for each horse wagered on determine the payouts for these multi-race wagers. The default unit for these bets varies from book to book, with FanDuel showing $0.50 payouts and TwinSpires showing $1 payouts in the Will Pays section.              The more races you put together on a ticket, the more you can win. But as with any multi-race wager, the more legs you add, the harder it is to win. In this way, these bets function similarly to parlays in other sports.  For some of the biggest races, the Pick-6 will feature a set guaranteed prize pool for the winner(s) no matter what the actual wagered amount is. The 2024 Kentucky Derby featured a $1 million guaranteed pool on TwinSpires for Pick-6s on races 6 through 11 at Churchill Downs.                           Understanding horse racing payouts             After the race, the winning payouts will be displayed for each bet type. The standard unit for win/place/show and exactas is a $2 bet. Trifectas, superfectas and super high 5s are typically shown as $1 or $0.50, but will say explicitly which on the payout board.              The payouts for each horse in the top three for the 2025 Kentucky Derby looked as follows:             2025 Kentucky DerbyWinPlaceShowSovereignty (No. 18) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$17.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$7.50 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$5.58 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Journalism (No. 8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								             $4.94 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$3.70 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Baeza (No. 21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								             				             $8.38 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				             If you bet more (or less) than the standard $2 unit, you multiply the payout by how much you bet and divide by the standard unit. For example, a $10 Win bet on Sovereignty returned $89.80, while a $25 Show bet on Journalism would've returned $46.25.              For the single-race exotics at the 2025 Kentucky Derby, the payouts were as follows:              2025 Kentucky DerbyPayout$2 Exacta (18-8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$48.32 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Trifecta (18-8-21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$231.12 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Superfecta (18-8-21-3) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1,682.27 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Super High 5 (18-8-21-3-20) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$38,405.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				            Biggest horse races beyond Kentucky Derby betting            The horse racing calendar operates year-round, but there are six events on the schedule that serve as the most important, thus attracting the best fields. The three Triple Crown events headline for the general public, but the Breeders' Cup, Pegasus World Cup and Dubai World Cup all offer massive purses and attract some of the best horses and fields in all of racing.             January 23, 2027: Pegasus World CupMarch 27, 2027: Dubai World CupMay 1, 2027: Kentucky DerbyMay 15, 2027: Preakness StakesJune 5, 2027: Belmont Stakes             Triple Crown of horse racing             The Kentucky Derby, Preakness Stakes and Belmont Stakes make up horse racing's Triple Crown. There are 13 horses that have completed the Triple Crown, winning all three events, and only two – American Pharoah (2015) and Justify (2018) – have accomplished that feat in the 21st century.              Not every horse competes in all three Triple Crown events. Each race operates at different lengths, and the turnaround time can be too quick for trainers to be comfortable running their horse in one after the other. Some Derby winners don't run the Preakness, while some have made it two legs before withdrawing from the Belmont.              The Kentucky Derby is a 1 1/4 mile race, the Preakness Stakes is 1 3/16 mile, and the Belmont Stakes is a grueling 1 1/2 mile event (although it is being run currently at 1 1/4 mile at Saratoga Race Course due to renovations at Belmont Park).                           Tips and advice for betting on horse racing             There are a number of strategies for betting on horse racing, but it all starts with understanding the horses and knowing their strengths, weaknesses and past performances.                           Racing forms and past performances             Racing forms are race-day publications and programs available at tracks and online to preview the day's races at each track. They are full of data and information from past races. All of the best horse racing betting apps have integrated much of this information into their betting screen.                           Track conditions             Before you even get to the horses, understanding track conditions is vital. Knowing if a track is dirt or grass, firm and fast or soft and slow, is critical information to know so you can look at which horses in a given race run best in certain conditions.                           Horse tendencies              From there, you want to understand the tendencies of horses in the field. Some horses get out to fast starts and try to push the pace, while others hang back and try to make a late kick. If most of the field is expected to push the pace and run it fast, then a horse that prefers to stay back may be at an advantage due to its advantage in a late-game run.              The opposite could be true, too; if the pace is going to be slower early, frontrunners are more likely to hold their position. Some of this information can be found in PPs or Past Performance data.                           Post position             Post position can also matter to a horse's success. Some prefer to run the rail (on the inside of the track) while others prefer being on the outside and running with more space around them. This information is all worth considering and comparing with the other horses in the field.                          Trainer and jockey information             A horse's trainer and jockey will also have tendencies. Some trainers are better at getting horses ready for a certain type of track, but maybe don't have a great track record at others. Some jockeys may be more or less aggressive on the track, which may or may not work well with that specific horse's tendencies, or they may have a long track record with that horse and know how to get the most out of them.                           Workout times             There's also plenty of data available that can help you. Workout times, if available, can give you an idea of how a horse has been running in training before a big race.                           Speed figures             Speed figures are like advanced stats of the horse racing world, offering a metric to show how well a horse has been running in its recent races that factors in things like field strength and track quality.              Taking all of that data into account is important to betting on horse racing, and for beginners it's best to ease in and do as much observing as you do betting. You'll start to find certain trends for horses, jockeys, trainers and tracks that can help you find edges on the odds board going forward.                          Manage your horse racing betting bankroll             Managing your bankroll with what percentage of money you have set aside for horse racing betting is vital to increasing your chances of scoring big at some point. Just like in sports betting, where most bankroll management experts advise no more than 2% of your bankroll should be bet on any given game, the same principle can be applied to any given horse race.                           Rules and responsible gaming             Responsible gambling is taken very seriously across all racebooks. What is a box bet in horse racing?  A box bet in horse racing involves picking the finishing order of the horses. Wagerers can choose the order of the first two, three, four, or five finishers, with the return on their bet increasing with every additional horse they include in their wager.
