title: NFL trade deadline: Ranking all 18 in-season deals as Kirk Cousins, Jeffery Simmons reshape Super Bowl race - CBS Sports
description: The Jaguars, Bears and Bills are among the teams that pulled off home-run moves
body:
The Jaguars, Bears and Bills are among the teams that pulled off home-run moves
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:27 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            12 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The fourth-most active trade deadline in NFL history is complete. Teams completed 18 in-season moves by the time the clock struck 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday as they positioned themselves for postseason runs and rebuilds. The biggest blockbusters that defined the deadline sent star defensive tackles to Super Bowl contenders and quarterback help to sputtering offenses, and those should prove with time to be the most impactful deals of the year.Some moves that occurred well in advance of the deadline have already paid dividends. Jeffery Simmons, for instance, is already a difference-maker for the Chicago Bears and was integral in their building a four-game winning streak. Others delivered mixed results, as is the case with the Quenton Nelson and Joey Porter Jr. deals since both players are dealing with injuries early in their tenures with the Seattle Seahawks and Dallas Cowboys, respectively. As for those that flew in just ahead of the deadline, the next few weeks will determine which teams won or lost their trades.Trades are about more than just coming away with more talent than the other team involved. Evaluating the impact of a transaction comes down to specific team needs, the capital sent back in return and how the move addresses short-term contention prospects and long-term roster outlooks.With those factors in mind, below are all 18 in-season trades ranked from most to least impactful.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Vikings acquire QB Kirk CousinsThere was one missing piece in Minnesota that, if found, could turn the Vikings into a force to be reckoned with in the Super Bowl race. It took until the last minute, but they found it. Kirk Cousins promises to give the Vikings the offensive lift they need to capitalize on their league-best defense. This year has been a renaissance for the 38-year-old who is on pace to threaten for his first 40-touchdown season. That late-career surge and his familiarity with the offense in Minnesota should allow him to step right into action and help the Vikings avoid the tight, low-scoring battles of the campaign's first nine weeks and start blowing opponents out. His arrival ought to also unlock Justin Jefferson and turn him back into the superstar-level producer he is meant to be.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Bears acquire DT Jeffery SimmonsThere is a strong case to be made that Jeffery Simmons is the best in-season acquisition, because he already proved to be a game-changer for the Bears. The impacts of the other trade deadline moves are speculative, while Simmons' is known. He wreaked all kinds of havoc over his first two games in the middle of the Chicago defensive line, was paramount in the Bears' win over the Seahawks and was one of the few reasons why they survived their five-turnover disaster on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 9. The three-time All-Pro turned the defense into a significant asset overnight. That is a transformational impact that will help this team maximize its potential with Caleb Williams leading the charge on the other side of the ball.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Jaguars acquire DT Jordan DavisThe Jaguars were one of just two teams to trade a first-round pick. They also packaged a 2029 second-rounder to land Jordan Davis. It was a high price, but that was to be expected, since Davis is a franchise-building block who signed a contract extension with the Eagles earlier this year and will be under team control for three years beyond this one. The trade should pay dividends both straight away and over the long term as the Jaguars step into their championship-contention window. It was about as big of a swing as Jacksonville could have made in the wake of the torn quad that knocked DaVon Hamilton out for the year. They did not just replace Hamilton; they upgraded.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Jaguars acquire S Jessie Bates IIIThe impact Jessie Bates III delivers to the Jaguars' defense in 2026 might be even greater than that of Davis, but he checks in one spot lower in the rankings because of the potential short-term nature of his stay in Jacksonville. The star safety is in the final year of his contract and may turn out to be a rental. If that is all he is, then the secondary will enjoy every minute of his half season in town, because as a three-time All-Pro, there are few defensive backfield stalwarts as talented as he is. Bates elevates the starting lineup but also minimizes the impact of losing Eric Murray for the season due to an elbow issue. Pass defense has been one of the few knocks against the otherwise elite Jaguars, as they rank 22nd in slowing teams down through the air. This helps immensely in that regard.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Bills acquire S Amani HookerAmani Hooker is tied for the league lead in interceptions and already has five takeaways for the second time in three years. That kind of turnover prowess in the defensive backfield through 2028 is worth spending a second-round pick and a fifth-round pick. The Titans captain has allowed a passer rating of just 79.3 this season, which is his best mark since his rookie season in 2019. For a Bills team that scores at will and just needs its defense to hold up its end of the bargain, Hooker's arrival raises the floor and the ceiling. Safety was a need after the Bills released C.J. Gardner-Johnson, and they filled it in an emphatic way.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. 49ers acquire DT DeForest BucknerThe 49ers' reunion with DeForest Buckner addressed a serious deficiency on the defensive line, where injuries once again reared their ugly heads. Alfred Collins and CJ West remain on injured reserve, and Gracen Halton just suffered a season-ending ankle fracture in Buckner's first game back in the Bay Area. San Francisco can seemingly never have enough playmakers amid its never-ending injury woes. Bringing Buckner back was more than just insurance, though. It is a step up in the trenches, which will aid the NFC West leaders as they pursue a championship.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Giants acquire QB J.J. McCarthyJaxson Dart's season is over, but the Giants' campaign is far from done. Even though the J.J. McCarthy trade did not make all the sense in the world when it happened, it has aged phenomenally, with the third-year quarterback stepping up as a commendable replacement for the injured starter. McCarthy is 2-0 as a starter and is playing the best football of his career (albeit in a small sample size) and has done nothing but keep the Giants comfortably in first place in the NFC East. This is not a long-term answer for New York since Dart will reclaim the No. 1 job next year, but if it allows the Giants to win the division and flip McCarthy -- or keep him as a renowned backup -- then it is a massive victory in the face of unfortunate circumstances.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Ravens acquire QB Jacoby BrissettThe jury is out on whether Jacoby Brissett can keep the Ravens afloat until Lamar Jackson returns from thumb surgery. On one hand, he has been a premier backup for years and should be far more capable of directing the ball in the way of Zay Flowers and Derrick Henry than Joe Fagnano was in his spot start. But on the other hand, the Cardinals benched him before they moved on from him. This was a desperation trade for the Ravens that, if it pays off, will result in them remaining on the fringes of postseason contention. If Brissett is nothing more than a bottom-tier starter, though, Baltimore can kiss this season goodbye.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. Seahawks acquire G Quenton NelsonQuenton Nelson underwent a minor knee procedure to remove loose bodies in his knee, which is a hiccup in his young Seahawks tenure and slightly downgrades the value of the trade. The expectation should be for Nelson to return within a couple of weeks and play at an All-Pro level. But he did not impress in his debut in Seattle, will miss at least some time, and is set to become a free agent at the end of the year, so the amount of time he spends making a real impact in the trenches could be slim when it is all said and done. The Seahawks need his supreme blocking ability in the lineup to help jump-start their dormant run game.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Cowboys acquire CB Joey Porter Jr.When he is on the field, Joey Porter Jr. is a lockdown corner for the Cowboys. But he missed his first game upon arrival in Dallas with an illness and missed time over the last two weeks with an ankle issue, and it is not as if the middling defense was all that much better overall in the four games he did play to date. Unless Jerry Jones re-signs Porter in the offseason -- and that seems like a stretch given Porter's demands and Jones' typical unwillingness to pay a premium to keep free agents -- this will be a rental situation. A rental with trouble staying on the field. It looks clear that the Cowboys were more than just a standout cornerback away from figuring things out on defense.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    11. Chiefs acquire WR Josh DownsKansas City would have had no excuse for coming away from the trade deadline without a wide receiver. Chiefs wideouts account for just 46.0% of the team's receiving yards, which is the second-lowest rate in the NFL. Josh Downs could help take some of the pressure off the tight end group and running back Kenneth Walker III in the receiving department and perhaps free up Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy to become greater big-play threats. In order for the Chiefs to truly be back to their Super Bowl-contending ways, they have to be more balanced on offense. Downs' arrival, at the very least, will not hurt in their quest for more passing production.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    12. Ravens acquire C Cam JurgensThe Ravens were in a tough spot at center when Tyler Linderbaum left in free agency and found their answer in early October when they made a play for Cam Jurgens, a two-time Pro Bowler and a Super Bowl champion who was part of the Eagles' legendary run at offensive line. Early returns on the trade are underwhelming, though. Jurgens is already up to 16 pressures allowed this year and was hit with multiple penalties in the early going, which is no recipe for success in an offense that has churned through quarterbacks behind him. Some of the troubles can be chalked up to the underwhelming guard play next to him, though.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    13. 49ers acquire WR Keenan AllenA rash of injuries devastated San Francisco's wide receiver group over the first half of the season and emphasized the need for even more bodies in what went from a deep group to a thin one in short order. When Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. are healthy, Keenan Allen projects as an ideal third option for MVP-contending quarterback Brock Purdy. He was the top-producing receiver in Indianapolis on a per-game basis, so he clearly still has something to give in the latter stages of his career. Expect Allen to command a sizable role in the immediate future before potentially giving way to De'Zhaun Stribling when he returns from injured reserve and serving as a depth piece and ready-made starter when his number is called.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    14. Texans acquire WR Marvin Harrison Jr.When the Texans took a shot on Marvin Harrison Jr., it made all the sense in the world. Their wide receiver group needed a No. 2 receiver to step up; the Cardinals were clearly out on him as part of their future, and he has tons of experience working with C.J. Stroud dating back to their time together at Ohio State. There is still time for him to turn his career around, especially since he remains under contract through 2028. But even with a touchdown in one of his first three games in Houston, Harrison has done little to command a consistent role. The Texans may have given up a second-round pick and a fifth-rounder for someone who will remain behind Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, Jaylin Noel and Tank Dell in the pecking order.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    15. Broncos acquire LB Daiyan HenleyThe Broncos should feel great about taking a starting inside linebacker away from a division rival, even if it came at the cost of two draft picks. Daiyan Henley projects to step back from his starting job with the Chargers and assume a rotational role behind Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad, so he will be a premier second-string option at the position on an already stout defense. This is the kind of move that will fly under the radar so long as Henley plays off the bench, but one that makes a rich unit even richer and gives Denver meaningful depth on the road to a deep playoff run. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    16. Lions acquire S Andre CiscoThe NFL's worst pass defense is a little less bleak now than it was before the Andre Cisco trade, but the move might not move the needle enough to make a meaningful difference in the Lions' inability to keep opponents off the field. Cisco can step into the lineup next to Brian Branch, but this has the look of more of a depth addition as Detroit awaits the return of Kerby Joseph. The latter's insertion back into action will do far more to improve upon the Lions' 260.9 passing yards allowed per game than Cisco. Joseph will either be activated by Nov. 17 or shut down for the rest of the year. In that sense, the Cisco move makes plenty of sense. But the Lions would, of course, prefer not to rely on him as a starter.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    17. Jaguars acquire DT Davon GodchauxHad the Jaguars stopped at the Davon Godchaux trade, they would have plugged a hole on their defensive line with a space-eating run stopper and pulled off a one-for-one replacement for the injured DaVon Hamilton. Of course, they proceeded to land Davis hours later, thus reducing the importance of the Godchaux deal. In the end, this comes out as a depth addition on a defensive line that is in flux but one that should be among the league's best at defending the run. Jacksonville is in a tremendous spot as it surges toward the No. 1 seed in the AFC.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    18. Ravens acquire OL Ryan NeuzilIt came as a surprise to see the Ravens make a last-minute move for another center, since they had already acquired one in Jurgens just over a month ago, but they landed Ryan Neuzil and pried him away from his starting job with the Falcons. Neuzil has ample experience at guard, so he could shift over to the left side of the line and replace John Simpson. He may also become the team's top reserve on the interior and one capable of playing at either guard spot or at center should he be thrust into action. Time will tell how the Ravens deploy him, and until then, the grade on the deal is incomplete.

body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline has come and gone, and while we did see a couple of blockbuster trades in recent weeks, such as the Chicago Bears trading for Jeffery Simmons and the Jacksonville Jaguars swinging deals for three players in one day, the final 24 hours of the trade deadline were relatively quiet. On Tuesday, the Minnesota Vikings brought back Kirk Cousins to replace Kyler Murray, and the Kansas City Chiefs added a new wide receiver in Josh Downs. However, there were plenty of other teams perceived to be "buyers" who stayed put, while other "sellers" were hesitant to part ways with their assets. In all, 23 teams combined to make 18 trades with 19 players and 34 picks changing hands. It was the Indianapolis Colts who led the way with an NFL-high four trades for six draft selections, although star running back Jonathan Taylor was not moved. So, who won and who lost at the trade deadline? Let's take a look.Credit to CBS Sports ResearchWinner: Everyone involved in the Kirk Cousins tradeThe Vikings and Las Vegas Raiders made the deal of the day, as new general manager Nolan Teasley sent a third-round pick to "Sin City" for Kirk Cousins. It feels like everyone is a winner in this situation.The Vikings are a winner because they absolutely had to do something at the quarterback position. Kyler Murray wasn't cutting it, and then Carson Wentz registered one of the worst performances by a Vikings quarterback ever on Monday night with an 8.9 passer rating and a 32% completion rate. The Vikings were wasting the efforts of the best defense in the NFL and found themselves in a spot where they were forced to make an addition. Bringing back a familiar face who has been performing well this season with 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions is a good move. 
Cousins actually has the most passing touchdowns (20) and career passing touchdowns (318) by a quarterback changing teams midseason, all-time. During his six seasons in Minnesota (2018-2023), he ranked top five in completion percentage, passing yards and passing touchdowns while going 50-37-1 as the starter. The Raiders are a winner because they got a third-round pick for their rental quarterback in a season where they likely aren't making the playoffs. The Vikings didn't enter this year expecting to trade for a quarterback in November, which allowed the Raiders to drive up the price. Kirk Cousins is a winner because he upgrades his own situation. He goes from 4-5 to 6-2, and has the opportunity to spark a legitimate Super Bowl run. That may sound like an exaggeration, but with Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson, the Vikings have everything in place to make a run. All they needed was better quarterback play. It could be a storybook ending for Cousins. 
Fernando Mendoza is a winner because he's the new starter in Vegas, although the No. 1 overall pick has to begin his NFL career against some aggressive defenses with the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday and then the Denver Broncos the following week. Another winner is Justin Jefferson, because he gets his quarterback back. JJ began his NFL career with three straight 1,400-yard seasons — including a 1,809-yard campaign in 2022. Jefferson barely crossed 1,000 yards receiving last season. Now, he can suit up next to the best quarterback he's ever played with again. His 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time (min. 50 games). Loser: Cincinnati BengalsTuesday morning, it was reported that the Cincinnati Bengals were sending a sixth-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles for pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie. This wouldn't have been a massive story, except the Bengals front office didn't realize they would also be giving up a third-round pick in the deal!
Nick Korte of Over The Cap pointed out that Ebiketie was signed as a compensatory free agent by the Eagles. The Bengals lost three compensatory free agents and signed two, with Cordell Volson not qualifying as a CFA lost since he hasn't played a snap this year. So, adding Ebiketie means the Bengals would lose a 2027 compensatory third-round pick that was coming after Trey Hendrickson signed with the Baltimore Ravens. 
From the NFL Collective Bargaining Agreement:"If a Club trades for a player who was a CFA during that League Year, whether the player was another Club's CFA or the acquiring Club's own CFA, the player will be considered a CFA gained by the acquiring Club and will be included in the Compensatory netting process described above."It's believed Cincinnati initially thought Volson counted toward the formula.Naturally, when the Bengals discovered this, they backed out of the deal. This isn't even the first time Korte has had to correct the league about compensatory picks. He actually helped the Bengals secure a top-100 pick in the 2024 NFL Draft after a compensatory mix-up.
Duke Tobin and the Bengals look silly because they almost gave up a third-round pick for Ebiketie. They should hire Korte in the front office after helping them twice in three years.Winner: Jacksonville JaguarsThere's no questioning the Jaguars' goal this season: They are all-in on a Super Bowl. Here's what they traded just this week:A second-round pick and a fifth-round pick for Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates IIIA conditional sixth-round pick for New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon GodchauxA first-round pick and a second-round pick for Eagles defensive tackle Jordan DavisJacksonville saw Eric Murray go down with a season-ending injury, so they targeted Bates to replace him. He's tied for the second-most interceptions (28) since entering the league in 2018 and is the only NFL player to have recorded a pick-six in each of the last three seasons. 
The Jaguars also lost defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton for the remainder of the season after he tore his quad, so the front office went out and acquired a couple of legitimate starters in Godchaux and Davis.The Jaguars are "winners" because it's exciting when a team gets this aggressive and pushes all of their chips to the middle of the proverbial table. Fans have all the reason in the world to be excited about this run for the No. 1 seed in the AFC. However, while Jacksonville's roster got better this week, I am questioning all the capital the Jags just spent. 
Trading second- and fifth-round picks for Bates is expensive, but giving up first- and second-round picks for Davis was shocking. He's a solid player in the middle, but no one had any idea the Eagles would fetch that kind of return for him. He's recorded 31 tackles and 1.5 sacks in nine games played this season, and he recorded a career-high 4.5 sacks in 2025. Just eight months ago, Davis signed a three-year, $78 million extension that made him one of the highest-paid defensive tackles in the NFL.If the Jaguars win the Super Bowl, then we can't complain about the compensation. But Jimmy James Gladstone is clearly in an "eff them picks" mood. PlayerTrade compensationS Jessie Bates III2027 second-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pickDT Davon Godchaux2028 sixth-round pick (conditional)DT Jordan Davis2027 first-round pick, 2029 second-round pickLoser: Running backsThere was a lot of oxygen given to running backs at this year's trade deadline. The Colts' Jonathan Taylor was a player everyone was watching, the Ravens' Derrick Henry was another big name brought up in rumors, theTennessee Titans' Tony Pollard was viewed as a potential target and Breece Hall had seemingly fallen out of favor in New York with the emergence of Braelon Allen. However, not one running back was moved.It's understandable if a team didn't want to trade a Christian McCaffrey-like package for Taylor, but what about Pollard? He shredded the Cleveland Browns for 129 yards and three touchdowns in Week 7, and then racked up 117 rushing yards and two touchdowns in Week 8 against the Bengals. He's averaging a career-high 74.4 rushing yards per game and ranks top 12 in rushing yards and rushing touchdowns this season. Pollard and Henry are the only players to have rushed for 1,000 yards in each of the last four seasons. Isn't that worth a fourth-round pick?There were multiple Super Bowl or playoff hopefuls that could have used a new running back, such as the Vikings, Broncos, Green Bay Packers and New York Giants. Instead, Taylor, Henry, Pollard and Hall will continue running the ball for teams that won't be playing meaningful football in January. Winner: Kansas City ChiefsThe Chiefs have the No. 2 offense in the NFL through nine weeks, but this passing attack has struggled. They needed to make an addition at wide receiver at the trade deadline, and Brett Veach did just that by trading a fourth-round pick and a fifth-round pick to the Colts for Josh Downs and a seventh-rounder.Downs has recorded the second-most receiving yards from the slot (1,995) since 2023, trailing only Amon-Ra St. Brown. While he's not exactly a "field stretcher" that is going to slice through defenses for 40-yard bombs, he still upgrades this passing offense. Mahomes is actually the only quarterback in the past 20 years to average under 5.0 air yards per attempt in four straight games (min. 30 attempts). Patrick Mahomes past four gamesAir yards per attempt20+ air yard attemptsWeek 63.60/0Week 74.70/3Week 84.70/3Week 93.60/1Loser: New York GiantsThe 5-2-1 Giants are the clear-cut frontrunners in one of the worst divisions in the NFL. However, John Harbaugh hasn't clinched the division just yet. The Giants did swing a trade for a new quarterback in J.J. McCarthy, but they were also interested in adding a star defensive tackle like Jeffery Simmons or a running back like Jonathan Taylor. Instead, they remained quiet on Tuesday. 
We'll see if Cam Skattebo can carry this rushing attack for the remaining nine games and if the Giants can finish atop this weird NFC East. But Giants fans wanted to see Harbaugh make an addition on Tuesday. Winner: Philadelphia EaglesThe Eagles traded away two starters in the past few weeks, defensive tackle Jordan Davis and offensive lineman Cam Jurgens. Remember, they also traded star wideout A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots in June. When you count up all the capital the Eagles acquired for those three players, Philly received two first-round picks, two second-round picks and two fifth-round picks. That's comparable to the Ricky Williams trade between Washington and New Orleans back in 1999.
TradeReturnRicky Williams haulTwo 1st-round picks, two 3rd-round picks, 4th-round pick, 5th-round pick, 6th-round pick, 7th-round pickJordan Davis, Cam Jurgens, A.J. Brown haulTwo 1st-round picks, two 2nd-round picks, two 5th-round picksLoser: Los Angeles RamsOne team that should have been in the running for Downs along with the Chiefs was the Los Angeles Rams. Davante Adams is on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, Puka Nacua is expected to join him with a knee issue, and Jordan Whittington was just placed on injured reserve due to a back injury. That means Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels are Matthew Stafford's top receivers. The 5-4 Rams are not the "Super Team" many thought they would be in 2026, and they didn't make any moves at the trade deadline in an attempt to right the ship. Sean McVay will try to grind out wins through Kyren Williams, Blake Corum and his tight ends. Winner: Buffalo BillsThe Jaguars orchestrated multiple trades to boost their roster with sights set on the No. 1 seed in the conference. How were the Buffalo Bills going to respond? On Tuesday, Brandon Beane sent a second-round pick to the Titans for safety Amani Hooker and a fifth-round pick.Hooker has been a beast as of late. He powered the Titans to their first win of the season against the Colts with 13 tackles and an interception, then picked off Joe Burrow THREE times in Week 8. Hooker is just the third player in the past 40 years to begin a season with 40 tackles and five interceptions through seven games. Following the release of C.J. Gardner-Johnson, the Bills needed to make an addition on the back end, and Hooker fits the bill. It was a pricey move, but I respect the swing from a Super Bowl-or-bust team. Loser: BTJJaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. was viewed as a prime trade candidate this year, but he's staying put in Jacksonville. A change of scenery could have done him some good, but BTJ will just have to deal with being WR4 behind Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Josh Cameron. His 117 yards receiving through nine weeks rank No. 7 on the team. 
Remember, back in 2024, Thomas became the fourth rookie to record 1,200 yards receiving and catch double-digit touchdowns, joining Randy Moss, Odell Beckham Jr. and Ja'Marr Chase. However, he's quickly fallen out of favor in Jacksonville. Thomas has played just 43.1% of offensive snaps this season and has caught zero passes in three out of the last four games. Winner: Defensive tacklesWe saw two big-name defensive tackles traded this cycle in Jeffery Simmons and Jordan Davis. The Bears sent the Titans two first-round picks and a Day 3 pick swap for Simmons, while Davis went from Philly to Jacksonville for a first-round pick and a second-round pick. Forget pass rushers, defensive tackles are the new premium position! There have been five first-round picks traded for veteran defensive tackles in the past two seasons. There have been just six first-round picks traded for all other veteran players in that same timeframe. Simmons, Davis, Dexter Lawrence and Quinnen Williams are the interior linemen who went for first-round picks in the last 365 days.
